title: Flight Path program sparks aviation career interest among students in Qatar
body_markdown:
**DOHA, Qatar, Nov. 24, 2026** — Under the patronage of the Ministry of Transport of Qatar, INJAZ Qatar and Boeing \[NYSE: BA\] concluded the first edition of Flight Path, an extracurricular program that introduced 74 students aged 15-16 to careers across the aviation sector. The program was delivered in partnership with the Qatar Civil Aviation Authority, Qatar Airways and Hamad International Airport.


“At the Qatar Civil Aviation Authority, we believe in the importance of initiatives that provide younger generations with greater opportunities to learn about the aviation sector and explore its various specializations. The ‘Flight Path’ program has been a unique and inspiring experience in this regard, offering students the opportunity to gain firsthand insight into the nature of work in the aviation sector and explore its practical aspects through training workshops and field visits. This has helped broaden their knowledge and introduce them to the diverse career paths available within the aviation industry”, said Mohamed bin Faleh Al-Hajri, acting president of the Qatar Civil Aviation Authority. “We highly value this initiative and our partnership with Injaz Qatar and all participating entities. We look forward to continuing this cooperation and supporting further initiatives that enable students to gain a deeper understanding of the aviation sector and encourage them to pursue careers in its various fields. These efforts contribute to developing a generation of qualified national professionals capable of leading the future of the aviation industry and supporting its continued development, in line with the State of Qatar’s aspirations and its ambition to strengthen its leading position in this vital sector.”


Through training in time management and communication, industry-led sessions and field visits to aviation facilities, students gained insight into aviation operations and the skills required for careers in the sector. The program included modules on aviation fundamentals, airline operations, airport management and air traffic control, all led by aviation professionals.


“We were proud to lead the Boeing module, introducing students to aviation’s role in economies, the principles of flight and different career paths in aircraft design, manufacturing and maintenance”, said Fahad Al Mheiri, Boeing president for the Middle East and North Africa. “We saw a great response from participants and hope their early interest will turn into long-term aviation careers, supporting the sector’s future growth in Qatar and beyond”.


Student teams presented projects developed during the program to a panel of industry experts. The program concluded with a graduation ceremony at the Qatar National Convention Centre on November 23, celebrating the participants’ achievements. Team ‘Altitude’ from Qatar Academy Doha, a member of Qatar Foundation, won first place for the best project in the Flight Path Challenge, which was dedicated to ideas for the airports of the future.


“The Flight Path program helped me to explore careers that I have never thought of following, that’s why this experience was so incredible for me,” said Leyla Huseynzada, a student at Qatar Academy Doha.


“The first edition of Flight Path gave students a firsthand look at aviation and helped them understand the skills behind such careers”, said Emad Al-Khaja, chief executive officer of INJAZ Qatar. “We look forward to building on this experience with our partners and giving more young people in Qatar the opportunity to explore careers in aviation”.


Flight Path will become an annual initiative, marking a new milestone in Boeing’s longstanding collaboration with INJAZ Qatar. Since 2009, Boeing has supported INJAZ Qatar programs that have reached more than 6,000 young people.


###


**About the Qatar Civil Aviation Authority**


The Qatar Civil Aviation Authority (QCAA) is the state entity responsible for regulating and overseeing civil aviation in Qatar, including air traffic safety, airworthiness and aircraft registration, in line with international standards. More information:[here](https://caa.gov.qa/en)


**About INJAZ Qatar**


INJAZ Qatar partners with the local business community, corporate volunteers and educators to inspire and prepare young people to succeed in the global economy. INJAZ Qatar is a member of Junior Achievement Worldwide (JA), the world’s largest organization dedicated to educating students about workforce readiness, entrepreneurship and financial literacy through experiential, hands-on programs. JA was set up in 1919 and reaches over 10 million students annually in more than 120 countries. INJAZ Qatar is also part of INJAZ Al-Arab, a network of 15 countries in the Middle East and North Africa united by a common mission to prepare and inspire young Arabs to succeed in a global economy. Founded in 2007, INJAZ Qatar has reached over 190,000 students from more than 100 schools and universities, thanks to 80 corporate partners and over 5,000 corporate volunteers and teachers. INJAZ Qatar offers programs in elementary schools, preparatory schools, high schools, universities and youth centers across Qatar. With the help of its active corporate volunteer community, INJAZ can reach students from Grade 1 to university. The corporate volunteers serve as inspiring role models for the youth, sharing their real-life work and entrepreneurship experiences and advice. More information:[here](https://www.injaz-qatar.org/)


**About Boeing Qatar**


A leading global aerospace company, Boeing develops, manufactures and services commercial airplanes, defense products and space systems for customers in more than 150 countries. Since Qatar Airways’ first Boeing order in 2006, Boeing’s partnership with Qatar has grown stronger. The company contributes to strengthening the local aerospace ecosystem, advancing innovation and research and building the skills and capacity of future talent. Boeing has invested $2 million in community and university partnerships in Qatar over the last decade. More information:[here](https://www.boeing-me.com/en/boeing-in-the-middle-east/qatar)
